title: Number a shared link's messages from a database row

blocks.text: Two gateway processes now share one terminal ID on the link to `acquirer-b`, so they need one sequence of STANs between them, and a Space in each process won't do. The sequence lives in a database table instead: one row per link, shared by both processes, and still there after a restart. The given `Table` class at the bottom of `src/main/java/com/example/practice/StanCounter.java` stands in for it. Each of its methods is one SQL statement.
Write `next()` in that file. The acquirer counts the gateway's duplicates and collisions, and it wants none, today or on the day the sequence passes 999999. About six lines.
One of the tests makes both processes read the row at the same moment before either writes.

cases.says: a link with no row yet numbers its messages 000001, 000002, 000003
the counter lives in the table, not in the process, so a restart continues the sequence
the six-digit sequence goes from 999999 to 000001 and is never 000000
taking a number is atomic across processes: two that read the row at the same moment still get different STANs

origin.section: 4.6 Each Link Numbers Its Own Messages

concepts: Each link numbers its messages from one counter that is atomic, outlives the process and wraps from 999999 to 000001.
